What These Tutorials Are For

  • Pastoral support and signposting.
  • A regular point of contact with your personal tutor (me).
  • A space to ask questions about the programme.
  • Peer connection and cohort identity.
  • Practical academic, professional, and wellbeing support.
  • No credits, no assessments, no deadlines.

Getting Involved In The Course

Getting involved does not only mean speaking first or speaking often.

It can include:

  • asking questions in sessions;
  • contributing to small-group work;
  • following up after class once you have had time to think;
  • joining peer study or discussion;
  • giving feedback through course reps;
  • telling staff early when something is not working.

Pair Introductions

Talk to someone next to you for 5-6 minutes.

Use these prompts if helpful:

  • (what’s your name;)
  • where you are from, studied before, or worked most recently;
  • what brought you to Behavioural Data Science;
  • one thing that excites you (about the MSc).

Then introduce your partner briefly to the group.

Settling In: Private Reflection

Take two minutes privately. You do not need to share anything personal.

Write down:

  • one thing you hope to get from the course.
  • one thing you are looking forward to;
  • one thing that would help you settle into the course.

Share only low-stakes points in the room.

If there is anything you would rather not discuss in the group but would like me to know or talk through with you, please email me / talk to me afterwards.

Useful Habits Early On

  • Check NOW, your timetable, and any module MS Teams spaces every week.
  • Read assessment briefs before you feel ready to start.
  • Keep code, data, figures, and reports in clear project folders.
  • For module-specific questions, use that module’s NOW page, Teams space, or lecturer/module leader first.
  • Use your personal tutor when you are unsure where to go.
  • Contact support early if workload, health, money, or caring responsibilities start affecting study.

Before You Go

You can:

  • ask a question about tutorials, the course, or where to find support;
  • mention something that would make these tutorials, or the course in general, easier or more useful;
  • raise a practical issue you think others may also be wondering about;
  • tell us a joke;
  • keep listening if you do not want to say anything today.

For anything personal or easier to discuss privately, email me after the session.
